newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia's Ollila positive on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Nokia's Ollila positive on EMU.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy sees Europe's planned economic and monetary union as a positive addition to the single market, Nokia president and CEO Jorma Ollila said on Wednesday.
"EMU will make it possible to benefit more fully from the internal market," Ollila was quoted as saying in a statement from the Finnish section of the International Chamber of Commerce.
"A well-functioning economic and monetary union would have a stabilising effect on global foreign exchange markets," he said.

"With the introduction of the euro, it will be possible to achieve significant savings in, for instance, transaction costs, reduced hedging costs and improved opportunities for managing cash flows," Ollila said.

Nokia is prepared for the launch of the third phase of EMU in 1999 and for Finland to join in the first wave, the statement said, adding it had decided to be among the first companies to begin using the euro as an accounting currency. @
Business needed a strong European Union capable of acting quickly and efficiently to create favourable conditions for companies in Europe and to secure fair competition on other markets, Ollila said.
